newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's creditors to support Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's creditors to support Hanbo.

text.p: A group of 61 South Korean banks and financial institutions with loans to Hanbo Steel Co said on Monday it would support court receivership to keep the steelmaker afloat.
A statement issued after a meeting of the 61 creditors said they would suspend demanding debt repayment by Hanbo Steel and resume overdraft facilities once the receivership is granted.
"We will continue to provide funds to Hanbo Steel until its steel mill is completed in Tangjin," Sheen Kwang-shik, head of Hanbo Steel's primary creditor Korea First Bank, told reporters.
Sheen said the creditors would also offer funds to suppliers of Hanbo Steel to prevent a chain reaction of bankruptcies.
The statement said loans to Hanbo suppliers would be in proportion to their loan exposures to the steelmaker.
The finance ministry said loans from financial institutions amounted to 4.95 trillion won, against its net worth of 224.3 billion won.

Hanbo Steel, flagship of the Hanbo Group, South Korea's 14th largest industrial conglomerate, defaulted on debt totalling 123.9 billion won between Thursday and Saturday, officials at the Office of Bank Supervision said.
Government officials said excessive investment in building the Tangjin mill with an annual capacity of six million tonnes was the main reason for Hanbo's problem.
